Breathitt County placed 55th in Kentucky for Housing Choice Vouchers assisted units in 2025
C. L. Foote
Breathitt County placed 55th among 117 Kentucky counties in the 2025 Housing Choice Vouchers assisted-unit ranking, with 69 assisted units.
Assisted units increased from 64 in 2024, a gain of 5 units.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally lower rent for eligible low-income households. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households describes three broad categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households receiving HUD rental assistance typically pay rent equal to 30% of their income after deductions, with the federal government covering the remainder. Eligibility depends on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are generally placed on waiting lists until assistance becomes available.
